central_bank_research.headline: BoJ raises policy rate to around 1.25%, effective 24 September
central_bank_research.summary: The 18 September MPM lifted the uncollateralized overnight call target to around 1.25% (from ~1.0%) by a 7–2 vote, citing approaching 2% underlying CPI, Middle East energy risks, and spillover into consumer prices; complementary deposit facility rate also set at 1.25% from 24 September.

central_bank_research.headline: BoC September deliberations: energy shock keeps near-term CPI elevated, limited pass-through so far
central_bank_research.summary: Summary of deliberations (16 September) ahead of the 2 September hold at 2.25% said gasoline-driven headline CPI near 3% could persist, upside inflation risks have risen with prolonged Middle East conflict, and governors would consider hikes if energy costs broaden into core prices.

central_bank_research.headline: RBA Governor Bullock: housing correction larger than expected but stability risks contained
central_bank_research.summary: In 18 September parliamentary testimony, Bullock said housing has softened more than expected, prices remain ~50% above early-2020 levels, negative-equity shares are limited, and monetary policy targets inflation/activity rather than house prices.

central_bank_research.headline: RBA Assistant Governor Hunter: rapid housing downturn within historical norms; oil shocks a key risk
central_bank_research.summary: Podcast published 22 September (recorded 7 September) reiterated house prices are not targeted, described the current downturn as rapid but not unprecedented, and flagged ongoing oil/geopolitical shocks as complicating the inflation outlook ahead of the next Board meeting.

central_bank_research.headline: BoE holds Bank Rate at 3.75% in 6–3 vote; energy path lifts CPI forecast
central_bank_research.summary: September MPC minutes (16 September decision) kept Bank Rate at 3.75% with three dissenters favoring 4.00%; staff expect CPI to rise toward ~3.75% in Q4 2026 and slightly above 4% in early 2027 on energy, while unanimously approving a gilt QT plan averaging £46bn/year to zero by 2034.

central_bank_research.headline: ECB September hike: energy keeps headline inflation above target into H1 2027
central_bank_research.summary: At the 10 September meeting the Governing Council raised key rates 25bp, citing August euro-area headline CPI at 3.3% with energy inflation at 14.3%; staff project headline inflation returning near 2% toward end-2027.

central_bank_research.headline: RBNZ lifts OCR 25bp to 2.75% on energy-driven inflation
central_bank_research.summary: The 2 September MPS increased OCR to 2.75% by consensus, noting June-quarter CPI at 4.1% (fuel-driven), expectation inflation stays above 3% through 2026, and openness to further hikes if needed to reach the 2% midpoint by late 2027.

central_bank_research.headline: Fed September FOMC: unanimous 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00%; SEP median one further 2026 increase
central_bank_research.source_name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
central_bank_research.summary: The 16 September statement and SEP showed a unanimous quarter-point increase, removal of accommodation language, median 2026 year-end funds rate at 4.1%, and Chair Warsh emphasizing inflation remains too high without offering explicit forward guidance.

news.headline: Oil rebounds in early 22 September trade on U.S.–Iran headlines and supply risks
news.summary: CNBC reported Brent November futures up about 1.2% near $101.54/bbl and WTI October up about 0.8% near $96.55/bbl early Tuesday, after Monday’s selloff, as traders weighed UN-week diplomacy against Middle East supply concerns.

news.headline: Reuters: Brent climbs back above $100 after four-session losing streak
news.summary: Reuters wire reports cited on 22 September showed Brent November up roughly 1–1.7% toward $102/bbl and WTI October higher toward the mid-$90s to high-$90s, with investors awaiting potential U.S.–Iran engagement at the UN General Assembly.

news.headline: Oil rises as Saudi export disruptions keep Hormuz supply in focus
news.summary: Anadolu Agency reported Brent November near $101.70/bbl (+1.4%) and WTI November near $93.35/bbl (+1%+) on 22 September, citing continued concern about Saudi export disruptions and broader Middle East supply risks.

news.headline: Monday oil hit multi-day lows on diplomacy hopes before Tuesday rebound
news.summary: Reuters reported Brent November fell to about $99.51/bbl (-4.2%) on Monday 21 September and WTI October fell about 5.3% to $95/bbl, the weakest closes in roughly 12 days, as markets priced possible UN diplomacy and partial Saudi flow recovery.

news.headline: Chicago Fed national activity index slips to -0.04 in August
news.summary: The Chicago Fed CFNAI for August 2026 was -0.04 versus a revised +0.08 in July; the three-month average CFNAI-MA3 rose to +0.01, consistent with growth around trend rather than recessionary readings.

news.headline: U.S. industrial production flat in August; manufacturing output falls 0.3%
news.source_name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
news.summary: The Fed’s G.17 release showed total IP unchanged in August after +0.2% in July, manufacturing down 0.3%, utilities up 1.8%, and capacity utilization steady at 76.3%.

news.headline: U.S. import prices rise 0.7% in August; export prices up 0.6%
news.summary: BLS reported August import prices +0.7% m/m (+7.0% y/y) with fuel -0.1% but nonfuel +0.8%; export prices +0.6% m/m (+8.6% y/y), highlighting persistent external price pressure despite recent fuel volatility.

news.headline: Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey still expanding but price indexes firm
news.source_name: National Association of Manufacturers (Philadelphia Fed survey)
news.summary: The September Philadelphia Fed general activity index fell to 37.8 from 47.4; prices paid rose to 48.6 and prices received to 31.3, indicating continued expansion with input-cost pressure.
